source.title_on_document: Harnessing GPT for Enhanced Academic Writing: Evidence from a Field Experiment with Early-Career Researchers in the Social Sciences

supplement.where: https://osf.io/f4epg (footnote 1: 'The pre-registration plan and all supplemental materials are available at https://osf.io/f4epg'), PDF p. 3 (printed p. 1)
supplement.holds: Pre-registration plan and supplemental materials; the main text does not say which statistics sit only there. Replication materials include the SakanaAI Python files (footnote 3, PDF p. 7).

paper_design_summary: At a three-day research hackathon at the University of Mannheim (Sept. 2024), run with Springer Nature, 22 doctoral and postdoctoral social scientists worked on their own manuscripts. After stratification, they were randomized into two equal groups: unrestricted access to ChatGPT (and any AI tool) or no AI. Five expert evaluators, blind to group, scored pre- and post-event manuscripts on six dimensions (clarity, coherence, depth of analysis, methodological rigor, originality, literature review) on a 5-point scale. The primary outcome is the post-minus-pre change in scores.

assignment.what_was_assigned: Unrestricted access to the commercial version of ChatGPT (and any AI tool) during the hackathon writing sessions, versus no AI assistance
assignment.quote: Following a pre-registered design, twenty-two participants were randomized to a treatment condition with unrestricted GPT access or a no-AI control.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 1), Introduction; stratification and equal groups: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 3), Participants and Design
assignment.prereg_locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 5), Hypotheses; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 6), H1-H2; PDF p. 3 (printed p. 1), footnote 1: https://osf.io/f4epg for the preregistration plan and supplemental materials. Preregistration is reported by the paper; the external registration was not inspected.

arms.name: AI-assisted
arms.description: Access to the commercial version of ChatGPT, allowed to use this or any AI tool, coached on prompt engineering. The paper says the 22 were 'divided into two equal groups' but prints no per-arm count.

arms.name: Control
arms.description: Identical tasks completed independently, without any AI assistance, under the same two-hour sessions. Per-arm count not printed.

participants.who: Doctoral and postdoctoral researchers in the social sciences: political science (14), sociology (2), economics (2), psychology (2), finance (1), policy analysis (1); fluent in English, only two native speakers. The paper states no separate analyzed count; the analysis section gives 'Given our modest sample size (n=22)' (PDF p. 8, printed p. 6).
participants.quote: We recruited 22 doctoral and postdoctoral researchers from multiple social disciplines: political science (14), sociology (2), economics (2), psychology (2), finance (1), and policy analysis (1).
participants.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 3), Participants and Design; n=22 in the analysis: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 6), Statistical Analyses

ai_tool.name_model: Commercial version of ChatGPT; the abstract says GPT-4 ('the first randomized controlled trial of GPT-4 in expert academic writing')
ai_tool.how_used: Participants interacted with the model iteratively during drafting and editing to generate text, clarify ideas, and refine written content, after coaching on prompt engineering (outlines, paragraph refinement, grammar improvement). PDF pp. 5-6 (printed pp. 3-4).

task.description: Writing and revising the participant's own academic manuscript (a dissertation chapter or working paper) for a special issue of Humanities and Social Sciences Communications
task.duration: Three-day hackathon with two-hour writing sessions; optional eight-week revision window for both groups

outcomes.name: Originality: change in expert rating (post minus pre), 5-point Likert
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Five faculty/postdoctoral experts independently scored each manuscript dimension on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = very poor, 5 = excellent); the outcome is the post-treatment minus pre-treatment rating. Experts were blind to treatment group but knew pre/post status (PDF p. 6, printed p. 4, Faculty Expert Assessments). Alternative automated assessment: SakanaAI scored the same manuscripts using identical dimension criteria and scales, blinded to treatment (PDF p. 7, printed p. 5, AI-Based Evaluations). Figure 2 upper panel plots the human-minus-AI difference in estimated treatment effects with unadjusted 90%/95% confidence intervals; the lower panel compares human and AI baseline assessments (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 9-10, Comparing AI and Human Assessors and Figure 2). Separate SakanaAI treatment-effect estimates and numerical interval endpoints are not printed; none are inferred from the plot. These are alternative assessments of the same participant manuscripts, not AI-versus-human-generated outputs.

contrasts.reported: Table 1, Originality: Estimate 0.11; t, unclustered 0.58; t, clustered 0.27; t, stratified and clustered 0.61; Westfall-Young adjusted p 0.87. Text: originality (estimate = 0.114, p = 0.875).
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 6), Table 1; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 8), Results

company_involvement.description: Springer Nature was the publishing partner: it helped run the hackathon and created a special issue of Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (HSSC) offering equal publication opportunities to both groups. The cited passages establish publishing-partner involvement, but do not establish funding or involvement by the AI vendor.
company_involvement.locator: PDF p. 2, acknowledgments; PDF p. 3 (printed p. 1), Introduction; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 4), Intervention and Writing Task

eligibility.reason: Randomized experiment with 22 participants in total (PDF p. 5, printed p. 3; n=22 in the analysis, PDF p. 8, printed p. 6), well below the 50-person threshold. Goes to the screening report's list of small randomized experiments. Criterion 1 is coded met because people were randomized to ChatGPT versus no AI, but the task is academic manuscript writing, which fits the creativity scope only through the expert-rated originality dimension. Criterion 3 is met through that originality score.

one_line_finding: With 22 early-career social scientists randomized to ChatGPT or no AI, the treatment effect on the change in expert-rated originality was not statistically significant (estimate 0.11, Westfall-Young adjusted p 0.87), while treatment effects on changes in clarity (0.49, adjusted p 0.01) and coherence (0.43, adjusted p 0.04) were positive and statistically significant on a 5-point scale (Table 1, PDF p. 8, printed p. 6).
